scientific_question: Does independently measured capture-time migratory readiness modify how landscape resistance is translated into later realised movement?
priority_design: project-aware Durif-stage x landscape-resistance comparison using open Europe-wide eel telemetry products

eligibility.taxon: Anguilla anguilla primary; other Anguilla spp. for replication
required: individual-resolved capture-time life stage independent of later movement outcome
response-independent landscape resistance or hydrological-opportunity covariates
enough cross-project stage overlap for leave-one-project-out analysis
reject_if: movement-derived migration flag is used as predictor of movement
FII is pooled into FIII to increase power
MII is pooled with female stages without an explicit sex/stage sensitivity analysis
landscape categories are redefined after inspecting the stage interaction
a single project determines the interaction

primary_estimand: Durif stage x WRS/landscape-resistance interaction on later movement expression
secondary_estimands: capture-time Durif stage effect on migration initiation
stage x landscape effect on migration progression or successful escapement
primary_cohort_note: FIII/FIV/FV are the primary cohort because each has >=98 individuals across 7 projects; FII n=17 and MII n=12 are boundary groups.
outcome_access_note: Aggregate successful-migrant counts by stage were inspected during development before v2 freeze; this panel is developmental independent evidence, not outcome-blind confirmation.
stability_requirement: report project-aware estimates and leave-one-project-out stability

interpretation.stage_only: internal readiness predicts movement but landscape gating is not established
interpretation.no_robust_interaction: do not claim the mobility-gating general principle from this panel

no_rescue: do not change stage grouping, WRS definition, or primary interaction after model inspection
